title: Performance pass: the shipped world, and one trade to call
question: The release profile buys ~4% of frame cost for +50% build time. Keep it, or revert those three lines?
context_md:
**This card is not asking whether anything looks different — it asks you to settle a cost trade.** Every change on the branch is *bit-identical*, proven by hash (`FIELD_HASH` over 3,900 frames, `plant_probe` byte-identical), not by the suite. The image is the real app on the branch via xvfb+lavapipe, confirming it still runs and renders.

**What the audit found.** Nothing had ever timed a whole `App::update` frame; the three numbers that existed were taken at three different world sizes. At the shipped 8192x2560, **with nobody playing in it**, the world cost **30.1 ms amortised against a 16.6 ms budget, 79% of frames over**. It is now 26.2 ms and 70.9%. Still over — the field is ~58% of what is left, plants ~28%.

**The trade I want your call on.** There was no `[profile.release]` at all. Adding one is worth ~4%:

| | field_cost | ascii stress s1 | incremental rebuild |
|---|---|---|---|
| no profile | 9.84 ms | 110.4 ms | 28 s |
| `lto = "thin"` alone | 10.58 ms | 111.9 ms | 23 s |
| **thin + `codegen-units = 1`** | **9.19 ms** | **105.9 ms** | **42 s** |

All of the win is `codegen-units`; LTO alone measured *nothing*. So it is ~4% of frame cost for **+50% build time**, and this repo values iteration speed explicitly. I landed it, but it is three lines in `Cargo.toml` and reverting changes no behaviour — your call, since you are the one waiting on builds.

**Two findings you may care about more than the 4%:**

- A **Rust upgrade can silently change how every plant grows**. `allocate_to_frontier` sorts donors with an unstable sort, ties are constant (mature cells pin at `RESOURCE_SCALE`), and the tie order depends on the standard library's implementation. An explicit tie-break would fix it and is itself a behaviour change — not mine to take.
- **§P's named lead is dead.** `body_index` cannot be `worldcrack`'s per-process variance: each id is pushed once per coord, and the whole path is the test-only liquid-body one. §P stays open; a fixed-seed hasher must not be sold as its fix.
